accent.note: Theme-dependent. Value shown is the default Purple theme; all eight themes redefine it.

accent-hover.note: Darkens in light themes, brightens in dark themes — the inversion is deliberate.

accent-subtle.note: Selection and local-user tint. The accent at panel weight.

bg-base.note: Page ground; also the recessed fill for inputs sitting on a surface.

bg-surface.note: Cards, panels, headers, modals, sidebar. White in every light theme.

bg-muted.note: The recessed tone — control tray, meter well, disabled fills, badge fills.

text-primary.note: Names, headings, message bodies, values. Also the PTT-active inversion fill.

text-secondary.note: Section labels, field labels, inactive control glyphs.

text-muted.note: Placeholders, hints, capacity counts, inactive nav, disabled text.

border.note: The hairline that does nearly all separation work. 1px passive, 1.5px interactive.

voice-green.note: FIXED — identical in all eight themes. A mic is open or a peer is present.

failure-red.note: FIXED — identical in all eight themes. Muted, deafened, at capacity, disconnected, destructive.

display.purpose: Join screen title. Once per screen at most, often absent.

headline.purpose: Modal titles and the room title in the header.

title.purpose: Participant names, room card names, the keycap badge.

body.purpose: Chat message content, empty-state copy, modal subtitles.

label.purpose: Every section header and field label. Uppercase, 700, 0.05em. The workhorse.

readout.purpose: Live numeric values only. Monospace keeps changing digits from jittering the layout.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Seated. Cards at rest, headers, control buttons, keycap badge.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Lifted. Room card on hover, mobile PTT button, reconnect banner.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Floating. Modals, sheets, participant popover, join card.

shadows.name: glow-brand
shadows.purpose: Accent glow under the brand mark only.

shadows.name: glow-primary
shadows.purpose: Accent glow under the primary button.

shadows.name: glow-transmitting
shadows.purpose: Green glow under the mobile PTT button while transmitting.

shadows.name: ring-selected
shadows.purpose: Selection ring on the active theme chip.

motion.name: default
motion.purpose: The system default for buttons, cards, inputs, badges.

motion.name: snap
motion.purpose: Settings tabs, theme chips, bottom-nav items — small targets react faster.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: The mobile PTT button state change.

motion.name: lift-hover
motion.purpose: Standard hover lift on buttons and theme chips.

motion.name: lift-card
motion.purpose: Room card hover lift, desktop only (>=600px).

breakpoints.name: grid
breakpoints.purpose: Room list becomes an auto-fill grid.

breakpoints.name: comfortable
breakpoints.purpose: Lobby padding, card radius, avatar size; modal centers instead of docking.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Chat panel loses its border and radius.

breakpoints.name: popover
breakpoints.purpose: Participant popover flips from beside the card to below it.

themes.note: The identity is the eleven-token structure; these eight sets are the worlds it renders in. Verify new work against at least Purple and Obsidian.

avatarPalette.note: The one sanctioned raw-hex set. A display name or room name is hashed to a stable index so a person is the same color for everyone, in every theme.

performanceMode.purpose: Applied when the tab is backgrounded. Force-disables every animation, transition, caret, backdrop-filter, speaking-ring glow, and will-change in the app.
performanceMode.constraint: Any motion, blur, or glow must survive being switched off by this class. State must be readable from color, glyph, and border alone.

narrative.overview:
VoiceRoom is a panel you glance at, not a page you read. Its users keep it open for hours in a background tab while doing something else; the interface’s whole job is to answer who is here, who is talking, can they hear me in the width of one look. So the system is built on restraint that isn’t timidity: the layout holds still, the type stays small and dense, and color is spent almost entirely on reporting state rather than on decorating surfaces. When something in the console lights up, it means something changed.

The identity does not live in a palette, because there isn’t one fixed palette. Eleven semantic tokens — three backgrounds, three text weights, a border, and a three-step accent — are redefined wholesale by eight named themes (Purple, Ocean, Rose, Amber and their dark counterparts Dark Purple, Midnight Ocean, Noir, Obsidian), and every component color routes through those eleven names. What stays constant across all eight worlds is the structure: the spacing rhythm, the radius ladder, the weight hierarchy, and the two status colors that refuse to theme. That invariance is the design system. Hue is the user’s; grammar is ours.

The component feel is tactile and physical. Voice controls are 48px squares seated in a recessed tray. The push-to-talk key renders as an actual keycap with a thickened 3px bottom border. Mobile controls fire a 15ms haptic tick. Interactive chrome carries 1.5px borders where passive surfaces carry 1px, and hovers lift a single pixel. Nothing announces itself, but everything answers when touched — and future work should push that physicality further rather than sand it flat.
keyCharacteristics: Eleven semantic tokens, eight themes, zero raw hex in component code.
Color reports state; it does not decorate. Green means a mic is open.
Emphasis at small sizes comes from weight and tracking, never from size.
Flat surfaces separated by hairline borders; shadow means floating or hovered.
Radius scales with the surface it wraps: 4px on chips, 20px on the mobile sheet.
Every animation, blur, and glow must survive being switched off in one class.

rules.name: The Eleven Tokens Rule
rules.body: No component may contain a raw color value. Every background, text color, and border resolves to one of the eleven semantic variables or to the two fixed status colors. The only sanctioned exceptions are the avatar hash palette, #fff as the foreground on a filled accent, and the rgba(0,0,0,...) scrims behind modals and the lightbox. A hex code appearing in a new component is a bug, not a style choice — it will be correct in one theme and wrong in seven.

rules.name: The Two Fixed Lights Rule
rules.body: Voice Green and Failure Red do not theme. They are the only two colors that mean the same thing in all eight worlds, and that constancy is what makes them readable as signals. Never re-map them per theme, and never borrow them for anything that isn’t a state report.

rules.name: The Tint, Don’t Pick Rule
rules.body: Status backgrounds and status borders are derived, not chosen, via color-mix in srgb. The established mix percentages are 8-15% for fills and 25-35% for borders. Never hand-pick a tint hex; it will only be right on one background.

rules.name: The One Loud Color Rule
rules.body: A single screen shows at most one accent-filled element competing for attention. The room card’s join button fills with accent on hover, not at rest. Filled accent is a call to act; more than one on screen and none of them read.

rules.name: The Shout in Small Rule
rules.body: Emphasis at small sizes comes from weight, case, and letter-spacing — never from size. A label does not get bigger to matter more; it goes to 700, uppercase, and 0.05em. This is why the whole interface stays dense without ever feeling shouty.

rules.name: The Tracking Inversion Rule
rules.body: Tracking runs opposite to size. Anything above 1rem tightens (-0.025em to -0.03em); anything below 0.75rem opens up (0.05em to 0.1em). Never ship a tracked-out heading or a tight micro-label.

rules.name: The Ellipsis Always Rule
rules.body: Every user-supplied string is nowrap + overflow hidden + text-overflow ellipsis inside a min-width: 0 flex child. Names are unvalidated and can be any length; nothing in this layout may grow to fit one.

rules.name: The Ten Slot Rule
rules.body: The roster is capped at 10 participants server-side, so every list in this system is bounded and short. Do not virtualize, do not paginate, and do not design an overflow affordance for the participant list.

rules.name: The Two Shells Rule
rules.body: Desktop and mobile are separate components by design. When adding a feature to the room, it must be placed deliberately in both — a change that appears only in desktop-layout is a half-shipped change.

rules.name: The Shadow Means Airborne Rule
rules.body: A shadow is not decoration and not hierarchy. It appears when an element is literally above the page (modal, popover, sheet) or is responding to the pointer. A surface that is merely important gets a border and a tone, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Scrim Pair Rule
rules.body: Overlays use exactly two established scrims: rgba(0,0,0,0.5) with backdrop-filter blur(6px) for modals, and rgba(0,0,0,0.92) unblurred for the image lightbox. Do not introduce a third.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Radius is a function of the element’s size and role, not a per-component choice: inline chips 4-6px, controls and fields 8-10px, cards and panels 12-14px, sheets 20px, status and identity shapes fully round. A new component picks its rung; it does not invent a value.

rules.name: The Chat Bubble Tail Rule
rules.body: Message bubbles keep 12px on three corners and collapse to 2px on the corner nearest their sender — bottom-left for remote, bottom-right for local. This is the only asymmetric radius in the system and it is what makes authorship readable without an avatar.

rules.name: The Mute Wins Rule
rules.body: When a participant is both muted and producing audio, the mute indicator shows and the speaking ring is suppressed. State that constrains takes visual priority over state that merely reports. This is a product invariant, not a styling preference.

rules.name: The Disabled Says Why Rule
rules.body: Every disabled control carries a title explaining the reason — Microphone unavailable, You are sharing, PTT Active. A control that is dimmed without an explanation is an unfinished control.

rules.name: The Recessed Input Rule
rules.body: Inputs and trays are always one tone below their container: --bg-base inside a --bg-surface panel, --bg-muted for the control tray and meter well. Nothing interactive floats above its parent’s tone.

rules.name: The Background Tab Rule
rules.body: A single class, app-background, is applied when the tab is not in the foreground, and it force-disables every animation, transition, caret, backdrop-filter, speaking-ring glow, and will-change in the app. Any motion, blur, or glow you add must be switchable off by that class and the UI must remain fully legible without it. Encode state in color, glyph, and border first; let motion be the amplifier, never the message.

dos: Do route every color through the eleven semantic tokens, and verify a new component in at least one light and one dark theme before calling it done — Purple and Obsidian are the widest-apart pair.
Do use color-mix(in srgb, var(--success-500) N%, ...) for status tints, at the established 8-15% for fills and 25-35% for borders.
Do reach for weight, uppercase, and 0.05em tracking when something small needs emphasis, and leave the size alone.
Do give every user-supplied string min-width: 0 + nowrap + ellipsis.
Do pair every disabled state with a title that says why.
Do use 100dvh and env(safe-area-inset-*) on anything full-height or bottom-anchored.
Do put new room features in both desktop-layout and mobile-layout.
Do keep interactive borders at 1.5px and passive ones at 1px.
donts: Don’t write a raw hex value in a component. The avatar hash palette, #fff on accent fills, and the two overlay scrims are the only exceptions.
Don’t re-map Voice Green or Failure Red per theme, or borrow either for anything that isn’t a state report.
Don’t place more than one accent-filled element on a screen at rest.
Don’t add a shadow to convey importance — use a border and a tone. Shadows mean airborne or hovered.
Don’t invent a radius. Pick a rung on the ladder (4/6/8/10/12/14/20/pill).
Don’t design an overflow or virtualization affordance for the participant list; it is capped at 10 forever.
Don’t use 100vh, and don’t let bottom chrome ignore the safe-area inset.
Don’t introduce a third overlay scrim.
